newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIA GAS OIL/JET- DIESEL STEADY DESPITE CRUDE DIP.
newsitem.headline: ASIA GAS OIL/JET- DIESEL STEADY DESPITE CRUDE DIP.

text.p: Singapore's gas oil prices, which have been rising over the past week along with the higher crude, remained steady to slightly lower when crude values fell on Thursday, traders said.
The stable prices also defied the 347,000-barrel build in Singapore's middle distillates stocks to 11.047 million barrels for the week ended August 6.

While swaps gas oil lost between 40 and 45 cents per barrel due to the lower crude and a $2.25-per-tonne loss on London's gas oil futures, sellers of physical cargoes remained optimistic, offering three cargoes between $23.00 and $23.30.
The higher number was for September 1-5 lifting, free-on-board basis, while the lower values were for second-half August.
While some traders said this was due to anticipated healthy winter demand, buyers were unimpressed with the high numbers after buying two cargoes in a row over the past two days.
Traders said South Korean refiners were offering into China at around $175 per tonne, cost-and-freight basis, but Chinese buyers were seeking around $170.
However, more demand was expected to emerge from the Philippines after Petron Corp had bought up to 400,000 barrels for August and September from a South Korean refiner.

Petron awarded the latest tender for 150,000-200,000 barrrels of early-September delivery at 80-85 cents per barrel above Singapore spot quotes, c-and-f Bataan basis. This would be co-loaded with gasoline.

Traders said Petron might continue to seek gas oil because the shutdown of an 85,000-barrel-per-day (bpd) crude unit and a 17,000-bpd reformer, originally scheduled for September 1-12, could be extended.

Jet fuel was offered at lower levels with four sellers seen at between $23.40 and $23.50 per barrel, about $1.00 below this week's offers. But traders said buyers remained aloof despite the more realistic prices.

Pakistan International Airlines has decided to award only one jet fuel cargo for now to Kuwait Petroleum Corp (KPC) at $1.25 per barrel above MidEast spot quotes, cif Karachi basis. The first cargo is for August 15-17 delivery.
The award for the remaining eight 25,000-tonne cargoes is being evaluated, a PIA official said.
